evidence.k1: One short living-composer piece on most programmes would meet the threshold.
evidence.k2: Include at least one film or game-score programme, or a half-programme
evidence.k3: Keep it and expand it modestly, for instance 8-10 nights, with players leading the programming.
evidence.k4: Keep Friday programmes close to the current mix so you do not disturb your 81% base.

evidence.k1: One living-composer piece in 12 of the 16 concerts would meet the rule.
evidence.k2: The film concert and Unbound sold out because the audience knew what they were getting
evidence.k3: Protect and expand Unbound... keeps the players engaged in work they care about.
evidence.k4: Saturdays (the weak spot): anchor on recognisable titles... Fridays: leave the subscription model alone.

evidence.k1: You do not need to commission to hit 20%, because plenty of existing living-composer repertoire is available
evidence.k2: "popular" does not have to mean "dead composers".
evidence.k3: Treat it as the pipeline for younger audiences... add nights.
evidence.k4: Your single-ticket problem is a Saturday problem... The Friday base is healthy, so don't disturb it.

evidence.k1: A 10-minute piece by a living composer opening a Tchaikovsky concert counts the same
evidence.k2: Keep one film-and-game programme, and consider a second... keep it to one or two nights
evidence.k3: Pick the strongest pieces from Unbound and move them into the main hall as short openers
evidence.k4: Saturdays carry the draw... Friday subscription slot can carry the more demanding commission
